pageInfo.subtitle: Master the advanced picking technique that creates wide interval jumps and unique melodic patterns through strategic string selection.
pageInfo.heroDescription: String skipping is an advanced guitar technique that involves deliberately skipping over strings while picking, creating wide intervallic leaps and unique melodic patterns impossible to achieve through traditional scale playing. This technique adds sophistication to solos, creates unexpected harmonic jumps, and is essential for modern jazz, fusion, and progressive rock playing styles.

items.text: Maintain precise pick trajectory across strings
Keep consistent pick depth and angle
Develop muscle memory for skip patterns
Precise finger placement for wide intervals

exercises.title: Basic One-String Skips
exercises.description: Start with simple one-string skips to develop the basic motion and accuracy. Focus on clean picking and avoiding contact with the skipped string.

patternNote.text: Pattern: Skip the middle string while playing outer strings

notation.title: One-String Skip: 6th to 4th String, 5th to 3rd String

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use strict alternate picking (down-up-down-up). The pick should arc over the skipped string without touching it. Start very slowly to develop clean technique.

exercises.title: Two-String Skip Patterns
exercises.description: Advance to skipping two strings, creating even wider intervals. This pattern is commonly used in jazz and fusion for creating sophisticated melodic lines.

patternNote.text: Interval: Creates perfect 5th and octave intervals

notation.title: Two-String Skip: 6th to 3rd String, 5th to 2nd String

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: The larger skip requires more precise pick control. Practice the motion slowly, ensuring the pick clears both skipped strings cleanly.

exercises.title: Mixed Skip Combinations
exercises.description: Combine different skip patterns within the same phrase to create complex melodic lines with varied intervallic content and rhythmic interest.

patternNote.text: Challenge: Varying skip distances within one pattern

notation.title: Mixed Skip Patterns: Combining One and Two-String Skips

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This exercise challenges both hands with constantly changing skip distances. Focus on maintaining even timing and clean articulation throughout.

exercises.title: Pentatonic String Skipping
exercises.description: Apply string skipping to pentatonic scales to create wide intervallic melodic lines that sound sophisticated while remaining harmonically accessible.

patternNote.text: Scale: A minor pentatonic with strategic string skips

notation.title: A Minor Pentatonic with String Skipping

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This creates beautiful wide interval melodies from familiar pentatonic shapes. Practice ascending and descending, focusing on musical phrasing.

exercises.title: Diatonic Scale Skipping
exercises.description: Apply string skipping to major and minor scales, creating melodic sequences that highlight specific intervals and add harmonic sophistication to scale runs.

patternNote.text: Pattern: G major scale with thirds and fifths emphasized

notation.title: G Major Scale with String Skipping Patterns

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This advanced pattern covers two octaves with consistent string skipping. Focus on maintaining smooth hand position shifts and even note clarity.

exercises.title: Arpeggiated String Skipping
exercises.description: Combine arpeggios with string skipping to create wide, harmonically rich melodic lines that outline chord progressions with sophisticated voice leading.

patternNote.text: Harmony: Am7 - Dm7 - G7 - CM7 chord progression

notation.title: Jazz Chord Progression with Arpeggiated String Skipping

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Each measure outlines a different chord using string skipping to create wide intervals. This is essential technique for modern jazz guitar improvisation.

exercises.title: Chromatic String Skipping
exercises.description: Use chromatic passages with string skipping to create tension and release in solos, adding sophisticated harmonic movement and technical challenge.

patternNote.text: Technique: Chromatic movement across non-adjacent strings

notation.title: Chromatic Ascending and Descending with String Skipping

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This creates dramatic tension through chromatic movement while maintaining wide intervals. Essential for modern fusion and progressive styles.

exercises.title: High-Speed String Skipping
exercises.description: Develop the ability to execute string skipping at high speeds while maintaining perfect accuracy and clarity. This is the hallmark of advanced string skipping mastery.

patternNote.text: Goal: Clean execution at performance tempos

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use progressive tempo training: start at 60 BPM, increase by 10 BPM when comfortable. Focus on maintaining perfect clarity at all speeds.

items.title: Technical Development
items: Start with single string skips before advancing
Practice pick trajectory without fretting first
Use a metronome for consistent timing development
Practice both ascending and descending patterns

challenges.title: Pick Catching Strings
challenges.text: Practice slower with exaggerated pick motion to clear skipped strings. Focus on curved pick trajectory.

challenges.title: Uneven Timing
challenges.text: Use a metronome and practice each skip distance separately before combining them in sequences.

challenges.title: Poor Intonation
challenges.text: Focus on precise finger placement and practice intervals slowly to develop muscle memory for accurate fretting.
